name: basten
author: animals-and-nature agent
description:
basten v3 (direction: animals and nature) — A FISH TANK, AND THE FISH THAT ARE NIBBLING THE WEEDS. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = THE EMPTY TANK, DRAWN, plus one number on a last line. Line 1 is the water surface, "~" repeated W times (W is 26-34). Then D water rows (D is 4-6), each W wide: "." is open water and "|" is a segment of a water plant. Each plant of height h (1-3) fills the bottom h water rows of its own column; there are 4-6 plants, at least 5 columns apart, never within 3 columns of either end, total height >= 10 with at least 3 plants taller than 1, and no plant reaches the top water row. Then the gravel bed, "#" repeated W times. Then a last line holding N, an integer 3-5. Whole clue <= 281 chars.

ANSWER = THE SAME TANK WITH FISH SWIMMING IN IT: the clue's picture minus its last line, with some water cells replaced by fish. A fish is "><>" (swimming right, nose on the right) or "<><" (swimming left, nose on the left): three consecutive cells of one water row, never on top of a plant. Everything that is not a fish must be exactly what the clue drew — same surface, same gravel, same stalks, same number of rows, same width. Whitespace is free (the scorer reads both clue and answer with .split()), so indentation, blank lines and trailing spaces do not matter. The depth is no longer a free parameter: the clue fixes it.

RULE. score = 1 iff (1) the answer is the clue's tank with fish added as above, AND (2) exactly N fish have their NOSE against a plant, i.e. the picture contains exactly N occurrences of "><>|" or "|<><". One clause: "N fish are nibbling a leaf — nose touching the stalk." Nothing else is required: any number of other fish, anywhere, either way round.

WHAT CHANGED FROM v2 AND WHY (the demo-economy pass, 2026-09-04). v2 measured 33% (25/42) under the OLD 6-round/6-demo format and then 0%/0% in the first 7-class run, with NO demo spent on it: both players read the clue "..2....3../4" as "a string plus a number", could not tell that the answer was a picture, and spent their three demos elsewhere. The rule was never the problem; the clue was.
 (a) THE CLUE IS NOW THE OBJECT. It draws the empty tank — surface, water, the stalks already standing in the gravel, the gravel — and the answer is that picture with fish added. A player who has never seen a demo can read the drawing convention straight off the clue and send a well-formed attempt. The old digit-string encoding of the plants is gone.
 (b) THE DEPTH IS FIXED BY THE CLUE. v2 let the player choose D in 4-6; that was a free parameter costing probes and teaching nothing. The scorer now compares the answer's non-fish cells to the clue directly, so getting the tank right is free and all the difficulty is in which fish to draw.
 (c) LOUDER DEMOS. solve() ships N+2 or N+3 fish (mean 63% of them nibbling, never below 50%), and every shipped demo is forced to contain: at least one fish whose TAIL is on a stalk and whose nose is not, at least one fish touching nothing at all, both orientations among the nibblers, and — new in v3, this was the v2 post-run lever — at least one stalk COLUMN that has a nose on it in one place and a tail on it in another, so the nose/tail asymmetry sits side by side in the same picture. No demo ever contains a fish sandwiched between two stalks, so "nibbler", "tail-toucher" and "free" are three visibly disjoint kinds of fish.
 (d) N IS SMALLER (3-5, was 2-8) so the count is one glance and the near-miss family "N fish beside a stalk, either end" lands in the foothold band instead of at 0%.
 (e) THE REJECTION FILTER NOW ONLY COVERS ANSWER STATISTICS. v2 also refused to let N equal clue-fixed quantities (plant count, plant cells, depth); those are not rival laws, because they are not things a player can choose, and excluding them only skewed N. Every shipped demo still falsifies: total fish, right-facing fish, left-facing fish, tail-touching fish, fish touching a stalk at either end, fish touching nothing, fish with a stalk one column beyond the nose, stalk columns touched by any fish, rows containing a fish, fish in the bottom row, fish in the top row and fish in the busiest row.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) The clue gives the object and the format away: it is a fish tank with weeds and a number. (2) A demo-less player guesses the fish glyph ("><>" is the canonical ASCII fish) and puts N of them in; scattered fish score ~0, fish tucked against the weeds score ~7%, which is enough of a gradient to keep probing rather than declaring the grader exact-match. (3) The demo shows a handful of fish, most with their nose in a weed, one with its tail against the same weed, one out in open water, and N equal to the nose count. The lateral step — the fish has a pointy end and only that end counts — is then a one-look observation instead of a statistic hunt.

WITNESS TABLE (500 fresh clues, 3 builds per clue; the attacker knows the format perfectly from the clue and builds a legal tank satisfying its own hypothesis).
 attacker's law ................................................ v3%
 clue returned unchanged ....................................... 0.0
 the clue's tank with no fish at all ........................... 0.0
 N fish anywhere ............................................... 0.0
 N fish touching a stalk, either end ........................... 7.0  <- the foothold
 N fish with the TAIL on a stalk ............................... 0.0
 N fish one column away from a stalk ........................... 0.0
 random legal tank with N+2 fish ............................... 0.4
 previous demo replayed on this clue ........................... 0.0
 one fixed real answer for every clue .......................... 0.2
 junk (empty / "1"*100 / half a tank / one row) ................ 0.0
 N fish snug on a stalk, one convention per clue (coin flip) ... 49.1
 N stalk cells nibbled, one of them from both sides ............ 0.0
 N+1 fish with the nose on a stalk ............................. 0.0
 N nose-on-stalk fish and nothing else (minimal witness) ....... 100.0
 N fish with the NOSE on a stalk (the true rule) ............... 100.0
Read the 49.1% row honestly: it is not an independent template, it is the true rule with a coin flip on which end of the fish counts. A player who snuggles N fish against the weeds all facing the same way is right half the time; that is the price of a rule a demo teaches in one look, and it is the main overshoot risk. Everything that is not the rule sits at or below 7%.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200 OK. 5000 clues: solve() scores 1 on every one, mean 0.76 ms, worst 15.7 ms (cap 2000). generate is deterministic and takes 0.036 ms mean over 200k seeds (cap 100). score is 377 chars (cap 512), 0.042 ms worst on junk (cap 50) and always returns 0 or 1. Clue <= 281 chars, solution <= 279 chars. The scorer was cross-checked against an independent re-implementation written from this prose on 18000 (clue, answer) pairs — real solutions, whitespace/case/reversal variants, flipped fish, fish over a stalk, deleted/duplicated/widened rows, stalks erased, the previous clue's answer, junk — with 0 disagreements. 1500 audited demos: nibbler count = N always, tail-on-stalk fish >= 1 always, free fish >= 1 always, both orientations among nibblers always, fish count in [N+2, N+3] always, nose/tail on a shared stalk column always.

LEVERS IF IT DRIFTS. Too easy (the likely direction, and the 49.1% coin-flip row is where it would come from): count nibbled LEAVES and require exactly one leaf eaten from both sides (v1's clause 3, currently a 0% trap); or count only nibbles on plants taller than 1; or count only the nibblers swimming right; or push the fish count back up to N+6 so the nibblers stop dominating the picture. Too hard: raise the nibbling fraction (ship exactly N+2 fish always), or draw two nose/tail pairs on the same stalk in every demo.
